{{nihongo|'''Atsuwa Shrine'''|謁播神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mikawa Province]].

'''Atsuwa Shrine''' (あつわじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Higashi-achiwa-chō, Okazaki|ja|東阿知和町|qid=Q17223219}}, {{ill|Okazaki, Aichi|ar|أوكازاكي (آيتشي)|az|Okazaki|azb|اوکازاکی، آیچی|be|Акадзакі|bg|Окадзаки|ca|Okazaki|ce|Окадзаки|ceb|Okazaki (lungsod sa Hapon)|ckb|ئۆکازاکی، ئایچی|cs|Okazaki (Aiči)|de|Okazaki|eo|Okazaki|es|Okazaki (Aichi)|eu|Okazaki (Aichi)|fa|اوکازاکی|fi|Okazaki|fr|Okazaki|ga|Okazaki|gl|Okazaki|hr|Okazaki|hy|Օկաձակի|id|Okazaki|it|Okazaki (Aichi)|ja|岡崎市|kk|Окадзаки|ko|오카자키시|lt|Okadzakis|mdf|Окадзаки|mg|Okazaki|ms|Okazaki, Aichi|mzn|اوکازاکی، آیچی|nl|Okazaki|no|Okazaki|pl|Okazaki|pt|Okazaki|ro|Okazaki|ru|Окадзаки|sh|Okazaki|simple|Okazaki, Aichi|sr|Оказаки|sv|Okazaki|tg|Оказаки|th|โอกาซากิ|tl|Okazaki|tr|Okazaki|tt|Окадзаки|uk|Окадзакі (Айті)|ur|اوکازاکی، ایچی|uz|Okazaki (Aichi)|vi|Okazaki, Aichi|war|Okazaki, Aichi|zh|岡崎市|zh_classical|岡崎市|zh_min_nan|Okazaki-chhī|zh_yue|岡崎|qid=Q242783}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}.

=== Overview ===
It is one of the two shikinaisha of {{ill|Nukata District|ceb|Nukata-gun|de|Nukata-gun|es|Distrito de Nukata (Aichi)|fa|شهرستان نوکاتا، آیچی|fr|District de Nukata|id|Distrik Nukata, Aichi|it|Distretto di Nukata|ja|額田郡|ko|누카타군|pl|Powiat Nukata|ru|Нуката (уезд)|sr|Област Нуката|tl|Distrito ng Nukata, Aichi|uk|Повіт Нуката|zh|額田郡|qid=Q787290}} listed in the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}*, {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=vols. 9–10}}. The enshrined deities are Chihaya-no-Mikoto and {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|fr|Kasuga no Kami|ja|春日神|simple|Kasuga-no-Kami|zh|春日神|qid=Q11088805|lt=Kasuga Ōkami}}.

The exact date of founding is unclear, but the *Montoku Jitsuroku* from the reign of {{ill|Emperor Montoku|ar|الإمبراطور مونتوكو|azb|مونتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|be|Імператар Мантоку|ca|Montoku Tennō|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر مۆنتۆکو|cs|Montoku|de|Montoku|es|Montoku Tennō|eu|Montoku enperadorea|fa|امپراتور مونتوکو|fr|Montoku (empereur)|he|מונטוקו|id|Montoku|it|Montoku|ja|文徳天皇|ko|몬토쿠 천황|nl|Montoku|pl|Montoku|pt|Montoku|ru|Император Монтоку|sh|Car Montoku|simple|Emperor Montoku|sl|Cesar Montoku|sv|Kejsar Montoku|sw|Montoku wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิมนโตกุ|tl|Emperador Montoku|tr|Montoku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Монтоку|vi|Thiên hoàng Montoku|yo|Emperor Montoku|zh|文德天皇|zh_min_nan|Montoku Thian-hông|qid=Q357225}} (850–858) records that “in the first year of {{ill|Ninju|Q1373077|qid=Q1373077}} (851), Atsuwa Shrine was granted the court rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade.” The *Mikawa no Kuni Shinmyō Meichō*, said to have been compiled from the late Heian to the Kamakura period, records it as “Atsuiwa Daimyōjin of Senior Third Rank”{{Sfn|‘Okazaki: Touring Historic Sites and Cultural Properties’|pp=223-224}}.

In volume 10 (Kunizukuri Honki) of the *Sendai Kuji Hongi*, compiled in the early Heian period, it is stated that Chihaya-no-Mikoto—a fifth-generation descendant of Izumo Shikishō, an ancestor of the Mononobe clan—was appointed as the first {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|es|Kuni no miyatsuko|ff|Kuni no miyatsuko|it|Kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造|ko|국조 (일본)|simple|Kuni no miyatsuko|vi|Kuni no miyatsuko|zh|國造|qid=Q2483673}} of Mikawa Province. Atsuwa Shrine is therefore thought to have been a shrine worshipped by the Mononobe clan lineage, part of the former provincial governors who held great power in western Mikawa{{Sfn|‘Okazaki: Touring Historic Sites and Cultural Properties’|pp=223-224}}.

In the early modern period it was called Kasuga Shrine, and records state that it was administered by the bettō temple Shōren-ji; this is written in the local gazetteer *Mikawa no Kuni Futaba-matsu*, compiled around the fifth year of {{ill|Genbun|de|Genbun|fa|گنبون|fr|Ère Genbun|ja|元文|ko|겐분|ru|Гэмбун|simple|Genbun|sr|Генбун|sv|Genbun|tr|Genbun|zh|元文 (日本)|qid=Q1145754}} (1740).

Until the Meiji-era {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, shrine rites were conducted by shrine monks from the adjacent Shōrin-ji temple. In the fifth year of Meiji (1872), it was designated a gōsha (village shrine).

Within the precincts stands a gate serving as the shrine gate, said to have been relocated from the “Nenbutsudō Akamon” of {{ill|Okazaki Castle|as|অ'কাজাকি দুৰ্গ|bn|ওকাজাকি দুর্গ|ca|Castell d'Okazaki|cs|Okazaki (hrad)|de|Burg Okazaki|es|Castillo de Okazaki|eu|Okazakiko gaztelua|fa|قلعه اوکازاکی|fi|Okazakin linna|fr|Château d'Okazaki|ha|Okazaki Castle|ja|岡崎城|ko|오카자키성|ml|ഒകാസാക്കി കാസിൽ|pl|Zamek Okazaki|pt|Castelo de Okazaki|tr|Okazaki Kalesi|zh|岡崎城|qid=Q1013445}}<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=https://okazakikeikan.boo-log.com/e117694.html | title=Atsuwa Shrine | work=Okazaki Iitoko Scenic Blog | publisher={{ill|Okazaki City Hall|ja|岡崎市役所|qid=Q11472848|lt=Okazaki City}} Urban Design Division | date=2011-04-04 | accessdate=2021-07-20 }}</ref>.

=== Festivals ===
In {{ill|Higashi-achiwa-chō, Okazaki|ja|東阿知和町|qid=Q17223219}}, a gagaku musicians’ association formed by volunteer parishioners has been handed down since the Taishō period. At Atsuwa Shrine’s three annual festivals (the Kinen-sai in February, the main festival in October, and the {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}} on November 23), miko dances and gagaku performances by the local musicians’ association are offered<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url= https://www.city.okazaki.lg.jp/100th/topics/p020876_d/fil/29iwadu.pdf | title= Okazaki Machi Monogatari 29: Iwazu School District | publisher= Okazaki City, 100th Anniversary of Municipal Incorporation Website | format=PDF | date=2017-1 | accessdate=2020-07-26 }}</ref>.

=== Access ===
* {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|Q6810397|qid=Q6810397}}
** Take the bus bound for Okuden Jinya, get off at “Aoki-chō” {{ill|Bus stop|Q953806|qid=Q953806|lt=bus stop}}, then walk approximately 1,500 meters east.
